summary: Phase 26 re-review after the 26.3 attempt-3 rework that closed attempt 1's single MEDIUM. The reworked from-phase-26 aggregate guard in scripts/check-agents.sh now recomputes every aggregate field from the phase's de-duplicated invocation set keyed by (role, execution.session_id, attempt): subagent_invocations_total and role_mix over the distinct set, phase_reviewer_invocations over the distinct phase-reviewer subset, task_level_* over the task-record invocations, phase_reviewer_* over the phase-only entries, and the unsuffixed triple = task-level + phase-only; the presence/equality check counts distinct phase-reviewer invocations across task records plus the phase record. I read the reworked section against the attempt-1 version and independently reproduced the required cases in /tmp/phase-26: with the real 26.1-26.6 records (17 task invocations, including 26.6's phase-reviewer) plus one phase-only gate reviewer, the semantically correct aggregate 18 total / phase-reviewer 2 PASSES; a double-counted aggregate FAILS in both the current-record form (19/3) and the pre-attempt-3 form the delegation quoted (18/3); a task-record-only phase-reviewer (17/1) satisfies presence and a recorded 0 against distinct 2 FAILS; and with AGGREGATE_APPLIES_FROM_PHASE temporarily lowered to 20, phase 20 (13/2) and phase 21 (56/0) still reconcile exactly, with perturbations proving neither is skipped. The attempt-1 MEDIUM is closed. One arithmetic nuance is recorded below: the semantically correct phase-26 count over the current records is 18/2, not the 17/2 in the worker's probe (which predated the attempt-3 orchestration entry), so the orchestrator must recompute the gate aggregate rather than copy the probe. The rest of the gate is unchanged and still met: scripts/check-agents.sh PASS (15/15) and scripts/check-docs.sh PASS (8 ok, dotnet-generated-block section self-skipped) on the current tree; docs/agent-contracts.md is exactly 220 lines; the rework commit changed only scripts/check-agents.sh, the A5 sentence in docs/agent-contracts.md, the 26.3 orchestration rework entry, worker-report.attempt-3.json, docs/plan/state.json's 26.3 reports list, and (newly tracked) the attempt-1 phase review; no product code, tests, artifact, or manifest changed across the phase; artifacts/ArrTags_1.2.0.0.zip is byte-identical and no 1.3.0.0 artifact exists. The tag v1.3.0-phase26 remains the orchestrator's post-approval step and is not created by this read-only review.

findings.description: CLOSED. Attempt 1's MEDIUM was that the from-phase-26 aggregate guard double-counted a phase-reviewer invocation recorded inside a task record: it computed subagent_invocations_total/role_mix as (all task-record invocations) + (every phase-reviewer entry in the phase record's subagents), so 26.6's task-record phase-reviewer landed in both sets and the semantically correct phase-26 aggregate failed. The attempt-3 rework replaces that recomputation with a de-duplicated invocation set keyed by (role, execution.session_id, attempt): `$pr_only` excludes phase-record phase-reviewer entries already present in the task-record invocation keys, `$uniq = [$inv[], $pr[]] | unique_by(invkey)`, counts/role_mix are over `$uniq`, phase_reviewer_* are over `$pr_only`, and the presence/equality check computes the distinct phase-reviewer count over task records plus the phase record. I independently reproduced: (1) the semantically correct aggregate over the current records plus one phase-only gate reviewer (18 total, phase-reviewer 2, role_mix worker 8 / reviewer 6 / tq 2 / phase-reviewer 2) PASSes; (2) the delegation's exact pre-attempt-3 numbers (16 task records + one gate = 17/2) PASS and the 18/3 double count FAILs with both the presence/equality line and the full mismatch list; (3) the current-record double count (19/3) FAILs; (4) a task-record-only phase-reviewer (17/1) PASSes and a recorded 0 against distinct 2 FAILs; (5) with AGGREGATE_APPLIES_FROM_PHASE=20, phases 20 (13/2) and 21 (56/0) reconcile exactly, and deleting phase 20's role_mix.phase-reviewer or inflating phase 21's total produces the expected failures. The MEDIUM is genuinely closed.

findings.description: The rework's recorded sensitivity-probe figures predate the attempt-3 orchestration entry and no longer match the committed task records. Probe d1 (the required PASS case) was recorded as '17 total / phase-reviewer 2' built from 16 task-record invocations plus one synthetic gate reviewer, because when the guard was fixed the 26.3 record still had 6 subagents. The same rework commit then added 26.3's attempt-3 implementation-worker invocation to docs/implementation/26.3/orchestration.json, so the current task records carry 17 invocations and the semantically correct phase-26 aggregate (plus one phase-only gate reviewer) is 18 total / phase-reviewer 2, with role_mix implementation-worker 8 (not 7). The guard behaviour is unaffected - I reproduced both the 16-record (17/2) and 17-record (18/2) conforming forms as PASS and the double counts as FAIL - but if the orchestrator copies the probe's 17/2 into docs/implementation/phase-26/orchestration.json, the aggregate guard will FAIL at the gate ('subagent_invocations_total: recorded 17 != recomputed 18'). This is a recording-risk note, not a defect in the guard or any task deliverable.

observations.proposed_change: In .opencode/agents/orchestrator.md's guard/delegation brief, require a recorded sensitivity probe whose inputs are the phase's own records to be produced by a scripted recomputation over the current records (and re-run/re-recorded after any later task-record change), instead of hand-typed expected counts.
observations.rationale: The first real exercise of the phase-26 aggregate branch is the gate record; a probe computed against a pre-commit snapshot is exactly how a correct guard reaches the gate with a stale number, and a scripted recomputation makes the probe self-consistent with the tree it is supposed to describe.

observations.rationale: Keeping a rework commit's scope equal to its named files lets the next reviewer verify scope from the commit without reconstructing which extra path is expected evidence and which is drift.
